chapter_title: The Oracle and the Algorithm, Part 1: The Oracle
learning_objective: The learner will explain the sequence of a Delphic consultation, from arrival to the written answer, by placing eight steps in a valid order and choosing the correct outcome at three checkpoints, with a valid order within two attempts and at least 2 of 3 checkpoints correct.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** delphi-consultation-steps
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Understand
**Bloom Verb:** explain
**Learning Objective:** The learner will explain the sequence of a Delphic consultation, from arrival to the written answer, by placing eight steps in a valid order and choosing the correct outcome at three checkpoints, with a valid order within two attempts and at least 2 of 3 checkpoints correct. **Prerequisites:** Pythia, adyton, pelanos, proxenos, promanteia, prophet, the Castalian Spring, the goat test, verse and prose answers (all defined in Parts Two and Three above, in "The Temple of Apollo at Delphi", "The Pythia", "Priests Who Framed the Answers", "The Oracle Consultation", "Fees and Sacrifice" and "The Oracle in Verse and Prose"). **Evidence of Mastery:** (1) The learner arranges the eight step cards and presses Check; an order is valid when it satisfies every constraint in Rules. (2) At each of three checkpoints the learner commits to one of four answers before the outcome is shown; an answer is correct when it matches the Correct column in Content. Mastery is a valid order within two Checks and at least 2 of 3 checkpoints correct on the first attempt. Reading the step descriptions after mastery is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) Anyone could walk in and ask at any time (step 1 and the consultation calendar). (2) The fee was the only cost, when sacrifice, travel and gifts cost more. (3) The oracle answered everyone in the same order (promanteia, checkpoint B). (4) The god could always be made to answer (the goat test, checkpoint A). (5) The Pythia always answered in verse (checkpoint C). **Instructional Rationale:** Ordering the steps makes the learner rebuild the consultation as a process with gates, and the three checkpoints ask the learner to predict before the answer is revealed, which is the Understand-level move of explaining why each gate existed. Feedback quotes the chapter's sources so the learner connects each step to its evidence. **Content:** The eight step cards, shown shuffled. The number is the order the chapter gives and is hidden until the order is checked. | # | Card text | |---|---| | 1 | Arrive at Delphi on a consultation day, usually said to be the seventh of the month, in one of the nine months when Apollo was present. | | 2 | Purify yourself with water from the Castalian Spring. | | 3 | Pay the fee (*pelanos*); a foreigner presents himself through a Delphian sponsor (*proxenos*). | | 4 | The priests sprinkle a goat with cold water to test whether the god is present. | | 5 | The goat is sacrificed on the great altar before the temple's east front; the day's consultations can begin. | | 6 | Wait for your turn: those with *promanteia* first, the rest by lot. | | 7 | Enter the temple, make an offering at the inner hearth, and put your question; the Pythia answers from the tripod in the adyton. | | 8 | Receive the answer from the prophet, write it down, and carry it home. | The three checkpoints, shown at the points named: | Checkpoint | Shown after step | Question | Choices | Correct | Feedback shown after answering | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | A | 4 | The goat is sprinkled with cold water and does not tremble. What happens? | The consultation goes ahead with a smaller fee; There is no consultation; The Pythia decides for herself; A second goat is bought and the line goes on | There is no consultation | A goat that did not tremble meant the god was absent. Plutarch tells of priests who pressed on after poor omens; the Pythia answered in a strange voice, rushed out screaming, and died days later. | | B | 6 | On the same morning, a Lydian envoy of King Croesus and a farmer from Attica are both waiting. Who goes in first? | The farmer, because he arrived first; The Lydian, because Lydians held *promanteia*; Whoever pays the larger fee; They draw lots | The Lydian, because Lydians held *promanteia* | Herodotus says the Delphians gave Croesus and all Lydians the right to consult first and freedom from fees. The farmer waits for the lot. | | C | 8 | It is about 100 CE, in Plutarch's time. In what form will the answer most likely come? | Hexameter verse; Plain prose; A written riddle in a sealed tablet; A nod with no words | Plain prose | By Plutarch's day the answers were given in prose, and he wrote a dialogue defending the change. | **Provenance:** Steps, sources and checkpoint facts from this chapter: "The Oracle Consultation" (steps 1–8, the consultation calendar, the goat test, promanteia, the Croesus worked example), "The Pythia" (Plutarch's story of the forced consultation), "Fees and Sacrifice" (pelanos), and "The Oracle in Verse and Prose" (Plutarch and prose). The order is the chapter's reconstruction, assembled from Plutarch, Herodotus, Euripides, inscriptions and the temple plan; the sim states "No ancient writer lists every step; this order is a reconstruction." **Rules:** - An order is valid when all of these hold: step 1 is first; step 8 is last; steps 2 and 3 come before step 4; step 4 comes before step 5; step 5 comes before step 6; step 6 comes before step 7. - Steps 2 and 3 may be in either order. Every other pair is fixed by the constraints above, so the valid orders are 1-2-3-4-5-6-7-8 and 1-3-2-4-5-6-7-8. - Checkpoints appear only after the order is valid, in the fixed order A, B, C, at the steps named in Content. - Each checkpoint is answered once for scoring. Score is 0 to 3. - Mastery: valid order within two Checks and checkpoint score >= 2. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner reads the question on screen and the eight shuffled cards. 2. The learner arranges the cards and presses Check. The sim marks each card in a correct relative position and names each broken constraint. 3. When the order is valid, the sim steps through the consultation one card at a time; the learner advances with Next. 4. At steps 4, 6 and 8, a checkpoint stops the walk. The learner chooses one answer, then sees the outcome and the feedback. 5. After step 8, the sim shows a summary: Order valid on Check number n; Checkpoints correct: n of 3. 6. The learner should notice that the consultation had gates (the calendar, the goat, the line) and that each gate could keep a consultant from ever reaching the god. **Feedback:** Order: on a valid order, "Valid: this is the order the chapter reconstructs. Steps 2 and 3 could come in either order." On an invalid order, one message per broken constraint: "Arriving comes first: nothing happens until a consultation day.", "Carrying the answer home comes last.", "Purification and the fee come before the goat test.", "The goat is tested before it is sacrificed.", "The line forms only after the sacrifice shows the god is present.", "Everyone waits for a turn before entering the temple." After the second invalid Check, the sim shows the order 1-2-3-4-5-6-7-8 and the walk begins. Checkpoints: correct shows "Correct." and the feedback text from Content; incorrect shows "Not quite." and the same feedback text. A running count "Checkpoints correct: n of 3" is shown. **Starting State:** The eight cards in a shuffled row, an empty sequence of eight slots, and the question "You have walked a week to ask Apollo one question. What must happen before you hear his answer?" **Chapter Anchors:** Eight steps in the order of "The Oracle Consultation"; seventh day of the month; nine months a year; the goat must tremble; Lydians held promanteia and freedom from fees (Herodotus); prose answers in Plutarch's day, around 100 CE; three checkpoints.
